title: FastAPI Security Utilities
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of fastapi security utilities in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to http authentication schemes.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers fastapi security utilities within authentication and authorization. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use fastapi security utilities to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is security boundaries, identity verification, least privilege and verifiable authorization decisions.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: FastAPI Security Utilities matters because it is part of authentication and authorization. In practice, focus on security boundaries, identity verification, least privilege and verifiable authorization decisions. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: HTTP authentication schemes
items.text: Use http authentication schemes as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: API keys
items.text: Use api keys as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: Bearer tokens
items.text: Treat bearer tokens as a trust-boundary concern. Verify identity and permissions on the server, use least privilege, keep secrets outside source control, and write negative tests for unauthorized access.

content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.
content_blocks.limitations: This code is inspectable lesson material, not executed by CodeLeaf. Run it only in a local virtual environment or a separately isolated runner with resource/time/network limits. Security examples are sketches, not complete production authentication or authorization systems.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “HTTP authentication schemes”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “FastAPI Security Utilities”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “HTTP authentication schemes” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for FastAPI Security Utilities, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.
